idea_en: Put up a clear, good-looking sign beside the road so that people passing by, and guests looking for the place, can see where to turn in.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 67 (PDF p. 68), Marketing – Sign
quote: It is extremely important that you have a clear and attractive sign near the road in order to encourage passing visitors.

idea_en: Make a simple leaflet with a sketch map, written directions to the house, a phone number and what is on offer; photocopy it and leave copies at arrival points and the tourism office.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
skills_needed: drawing a sketch map, basic writing, access to a photocopier
page: p. 68 (PDF p. 69), Brochures and Business cards
quote: You might like to try to produce a simple brochure which you could be photocopied and left at the airport, provincial tourism bureau.
quote_2: Your name and telephone number • An attractive sketch, picture or map • Directions about how to get to your guesthouse and • A list of your facilities and activities.

idea_en: Ask guests the evening before which kind of breakfast they want (local or the style they are used to), so it can be ready in the morning without guessing.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 29 (PDF p. 30), Menu planning – Breakfast
quote: Ask them the night before if your guests prefer a PNG or European breakfast

idea_en: Tell guests the meal times, and when only a few guests are staying, ask what time they would like to eat and fit meals around that.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 33 (PDF p. 34), Food serving
quote: If you only have a few guests ask what time they prefer to eat and try to cater to their needs.
quote_2: Let guests know what time meals are served.

idea_en: When there is no choice of dishes, write the day's menu up each morning in the dining area (a chalk or white board works) so guests know what is coming.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 28 (PDF p. 29), Menu planning
quote: If you are not able to give a choice of food make sure to put up a menu every morning in the dining area for guests to see.

idea_en: Turn meals into an experience: walk guests through the food garden, let them watch the cooking and try the local recipes themselves.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 34 (PDF p. 35), Food serving
quote: You might also like to show your guests your food garden and encourage them to try local recipes and see how the food is prepared.

idea_en: Keep a board in the common area listing each activity on offer with its price, so guests can see at any time what they can do and what it costs.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 40 (PDF p. 41), Informing guests about activities
quote: You could have a white/black board located in the common area where you could have a list of the different activities and their prices.

idea_en: A rural tour service lets visitors spend an afternoon doing real farm work – in the rice field or gathering wild vegetables – as part of their stay.
where: Sakae Mura, Nagano, Japan (One Life Japan case study)
skills_needed: farming know-how the host already has
source_title: Effective Community Based Tourism: A Best Practice Manual, June 2010 (APEC)
page: p. 118 (PDF p. 131), 9.12 Case Study: One Life, Japan
quote: They can set off hiking in the countryside on their own, or work for an afternoon in a rice field or collecting wild vegetables.

idea_en: Make hand-washing with soap the fixed first step before anyone touches food; the same checklist also asks for clean utensils and separate boards and knives for meat and vegetables.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 32 (PDF p. 33), Food preparation
quote: Always wash your hands with soap before touching any food
quote_2: Prepare meat and vegetables on different cutting boards and with different knives and wash the utensils well afterwards

idea_en: Give guests only boiled drinking water: boil it for at least ten minutes, then store it in a clean container and keep it cool.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 30 (PDF p. 31), Drinks and snacks
quote: This drinking water must be boiled for at least ten minutes to remove bacteria and then placed in a clean container cooled and placed in the fridge.

idea_en: Keep food covered once it is served, and serve guests only safe drinking water.
where: general guideline (ASEAN member states)
page: p. 9 (PDF p. 21), §5.6.3.6 Food Preparation
quote: Served food shall be properly covered.
quote_2: Guests shall only be served safe drinking water.

idea_en: Have one person do the welcome: greet guests in the host's own language, and where a family member has some English, let that person explain how things work.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
skills_needed: one family member with some English
page: p. 9 (PDF p. 10), Meeting and Greeting – Welcoming
quote: Greeting tourists in your own language will add to their experience, if there is someone in the family who speaks some English and can explain everything

idea_en: When the English speaker is away, whoever answers the phone uses a short memorised script: take the caller's name and number and promise a call back.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 24 (PDF p. 25), Booking Facilities
quote: the person who answers the phone would be able to at least ask for a name and a telephone number and say “My mother will call you back later”

idea_en: A rural tour service makes bilingual helpers who know the area and culture available to visitors, bridging between guests and local families.
where: Sakae Mura, Nagano, Japan (One Life Japan case study)
skills_needed: a bilingual person who knows the area
source_title: Effective Community Based Tourism: A Best Practice Manual, June 2010 (APEC)
page: p. 118 (PDF p. 131), 9.12 Case Study: One Life, Japan
quote: Bilingual facilitators who have studied the area and culture are available

idea_en: Get listed in a travel guidebook: a remote lodge without internet access found that a guidebook listing was what spread the word and brought steady growth.
where: Kumul Lodge, Highlands, Papua New Guinea
skills_needed: contacting guidebook publishers / hosting a travel writer
source_title: Effective Community Based Tourism: A Best Practice Manual, June 2010 (APEC)
page: p. 115 (PDF p. 128), 9.10 Case Study: Kumul Lodge – Challenges faced
quote: A listing in the Lonely Planet was crucial in spreading the word about the lodge and since then it has consistently grown.
quote_2: The remote location of Kumul Lodge has meant that it faces many communication-based challenges. The lack of Internet access makes it difficult to attract international visitors.

idea_en: List the place on travel websites and social media – directly or through the tourism authority – and answer negative comments quickly.
where: general guideline (APEC economies)
skills_needed: basic internet and social media use
source_title: Effective Community Based Tourism: A Best Practice Manual, June 2010 (APEC)
page: p. 71 (PDF p. 84), 7.4 – Get online and network
quote: Community managers or tourism authorities can list the destination on travel websites and make use of social networking and media sites to promote CBT (e.g. Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, Flickr).
quote_2: It is important to recognise that anyone can post on these online travel networks and negative comments need to be addressed swiftly.

idea_en: Ask young people in the village to look after the homestay's website and social media pages and keep them up to date.
where: general guideline (ASEAN member states)
skills_needed: a young person comfortable with social media
page: p. 10 (PDF p. 22), §5.8.3.2 Web Marketing
quote: It is recommended to engage the village youth to maintain and update the online promotional mediums.

idea_en: Give guests a short safety briefing before every activity starts.
where: general guideline (ASEAN member states)
skills_needed: knowing the risks of each activity
page: p. 10 (PDF p. 22), §5.7.3.1 Briefing on Safety Aspects
quote: Guests shall be briefed on safety aspects prior to taking part in any homestay activity.

idea_en: Make sure at least one family member has first aid training so that someone on site can respond if a guest is hurt.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 51 (PDF p. 52), Guest Safety
quote: Try to make sure one of your family is trained in first aid procedures

idea_en: Ban candles in guest rooms and show guests how to use any lamps safely.
where: Papua New Guinea (guidebook advice for village guesthouses)
page: p. 48 (PDF p. 49), Site Security – Fire
quote: Do not allow the use of candles in guesthouses as these pose a big fire hazard.
quote_2: If you provide kerosene lamps or BBQ facilities for your guests show them how these can be safely used.

idea_en: On the day guests leave, send them a message asking them to review their stay.
where: general guideline (Airbnb)
skills_needed: sending a phone message in a language the guest reads
source_title: How to welcome your first Airbnb guests (Airbnb Resource Center)
page: web page, section on reviews (last section)
quote: Consider scheduling a message on the day of checkout asking guests to review their stay.

idea_en: After guests leave, write a review of them: use it to thank them, give feedback and remind them to review you.
where: general guideline (Airbnb)
skills_needed: writing a short review on a booking site
page: web page, Step 5: Giving and getting reviews
quote: Review your guests. This is a chance to express gratitude, share feedback and remind guests to review you.

idea_en: Reply to the reviews guests leave, and use the reply to show you are open to improving.
where: general guideline (Airbnb)
skills_needed: reading and answering reviews on a booking site
page: web page, Step 5: Giving and getting reviews
quote: Respond to reviews. Use this as an opportunity to show you’re open to improving.

idea_en: A host treats what guests say in reviews as her guide to improving, and takes it to heart.
where: Santa Fe, New Mexico, USA (host quoted by Airbnb)
page: web page, Step 5: Giving and getting reviews
quote: “It’s important to take reviews to heart,” says Sadie, a Superhost in Santa Fe, New Mexico.
quote_2: “Guests are really your guide to getting to five stars.”

idea_en: Give arrival instructions one step at a time, and add photos or a map with arrows.
where: general guideline (Airbnb)
skills_needed: drawing a simple map or taking photos; a way to get them to guests before they arrive
page: web page, Step 2: Making check-in and checkout a breeze
quote: Write clear check-in instructions. Explain the process step by step, and include any details that might be helpful, such as photos or a map with arrows.

idea_en: Small gestures count: for example leave a blanket out for guests, or share some coffee or tea with them.
where: general guideline (Airbnb)
page: web page, section on paying attention to details
quote: Small gestures go a long way, like leaving a blanket on a couch or sharing some coffee or tea.

idea_en: Keep a fire extinguisher, a first-aid kit and a torch ready, and give guests the emergency phone numbers.
where: general guideline (Airbnb)
page: web page, Step 4: Preparing for the unexpected
quote: Equip your space with a fire extinguisher, first-aid kit and torch. Share emergency phone numbers in the event guests need help.

idea_en: Before guests arrive, make sure the basics are there: towels, bed linen, pillows, soap and toilet paper.
where: general guideline (Airbnb)
source_title: How to welcome your first Airbnb guests (Airbnb Resource Center)
page: web page, section on providing a comfortable stay
quote: Stock up on the basics. These include towels, linens, pillows, soap, and toilet paper.

idea_en: A homestay host grows seasonal and off-season vegetables all year round and serves her guests food made from her own farm's produce.
where: Tusse village, Kaski, Nepal
source_title: Gurung family's homestay : Home away from home (Caritas Nepal)
page: web page
quote: Ms. Bankumri Gurung has been farming different types of seasonal and off seasonal vegetables all year round to serve her guests from homestay.
quote_2: They serve tasty delicacies prepared from organic products from their farm.

idea_en: A homestay village is described as having neat and tidy houses, with toilets and drinking water facilities.
where: Sirubari, Syangja, Nepal
skills_needed: keeping the house tidy; a toilet and a drinking water supply
source_title: Homestay business spread from Sirubari (Kantipur, AI-translated English page)
page: web page — page description only (the article body did not load)
quote: Neat and tidy houses, toilets and drinking water facilities like in a developed city, clean and spacious stone paved streets.
